assessment: All 14 retained main-PDF pages read and visually inspected, including raster text and tables omitted by native extraction. Fifteen figures, six tables, eleven printed correlations, captions/legends, eight bibliography entries and five additional dependencies are recorded. Small MEM tracks, maps and tables were enlarged; unresolved tiny labels and exact data mappings remain qualified. The 77 checks are limited arithmetic and analyst examples, not full model reproduction. Cited originals, native tests/field/model arrays, full failure/creep/coupling derivations and external assets remain open. No comprehensive completion or annual-service calibration.

sections.assessment: PETRONAS authors; IPTC-19491-MS, Beijing, 26–28 March 2019. The header reports abstract selection and says contents were not reviewed by IPTC. The abstract promises cost/time benefits and different injection plans without a comparative cost/time baseline, numeric storage capacity or complete scenario comparison. The UTM download watermark dated 31 October 2026 is access provenance, not a field-observation date.

Central Luconia offshore Sarawak carbonate gas build-up over an aquifer; production began in 1995. Platform GPS history motivates subsidence, lateral movement, fault and caprock assessment. Planned CO2 comes from nearby high-CO2 gas fields. The field name, imported-CO2 access, rates, capture/transport inventory and current operating status are not established.

Four wells X-1 to X-4 selected by sonic availability/quality. Dynamic-to-static elasticity calibration, in-house regional strength correlations, lithology-specific drilling matches, poroelastic horizontal strain, LOT calibration and regional stress orientation are described. Raw logs/LOT values, complete formulas, sample errors and independent validation sets are absent. The normal-to-strike-slip interpretation cannot be reconstructed from full stresses.

Reservoir/aquifer extended to overburden, sideburden and underburden; approximately two million cells. Eleven empirical correlations in Tables 1–2 support the ISAMGEO critical-state/cap/creep model. Field porosity arrays, input scale and fit range, dimensions, Biot coefficient, yield/flow/creep integration and convergence evidence are missing.

Kriging uses four MEMs; Figure 6 compares populated and source properties at those wells. Stress boundaries are iterated with gravity, pore-pressure forces and horizontal loading. Sh at 110° is orthogonal to SH at N20°E if conventions agree. Full vertical stress, pressure datum and boundary constraints are missing. A calibration comparison is not independent validation.

Twenty-three selected history/forecast pressure states, with denser sampling during depletion/aquifer history. Depletion ends in 2003; injection is proposed for 2024–2040. Pore-collapse/creep parameters are adjusted within laboratory ranges against GPS. Selected-state counts do not provide annual flow or full injection controls.

Predictions: 9.6 ft in 2003, 11.3 ft in 2013 versus GPS 11.65 ft in 2014, about 1 ft injection uplift, and final 10.6 ft seabed subsidence/16 ft reservoir compaction. Platform histories, spatial maxima and epochs differ. The 2002–2012 bathymetry comparison is qualitative; registration, datum, errors and independent validation statistics are not supplied.

The selected critical-state model cannot compute plastic strain along frictional elements, so deformation is used as a workaround. In the absence of fault samples, properties from a nearby SF-30 clastic analogue are adopted for carbonate Field X. Tables 4–5 and Figures 11–13 were inspected. Four named/displayed faults versus five in the conclusion is unresolved. Page 11 expressly excludes a cement-bond/casing-caprock leakage pathway; that sentence is omitted by native extraction.

About 2% highest local plastic strain occurs at the crest with porosity above 30%. Foreign-field average and incremental-average compaction strains are compared, despite different metrics. Small injection-phase increments are conditional model results. Reported Shmin is 4,600–6,200 psi; a 4,000 psi reservoir recommendation has a 600 psi difference from the lower endpoint. Full fracture and leakage models are unavailable.

Conclusions repeat the GPS match, final deformation, local crest damage, approximately 0.5 cm slip, five affected faults and recommended pressure. No independent uncertainty, annual rate, retained-carbon horizon or quantitative study-cost/time improvement is established. The forecast is not evidence that injection occurred in 2024.

Eight printed entries inspected, including text omitted by native extraction. Table/body years 2014/2002 differ from bibliography 2013/2012; Tjia geographic support needs the original. SF-30 is reported in Sabah in Tables 4–5; Sarawak Shell in the bibliography is an operator name, not conflicting field-location evidence. Five additional data/model/method dependencies are tracked. No exact retained originals were established; all underlying sources remain unverified.

Every row and unit transcribed as E01–E07. Phi scale and validity range are unspecified. Fraction/percent comparisons are analyst examples; no field sample is invented. Fitted correlations and prescribed ratios are not derivations of a constitutive model.

All fields, reservoir types, normal/shear stiffness (psi/ft), cohesion (psi) and friction (degrees) retained in inputs. Pereira stiffness dashes remain null. Analogues: Ekofisk chalk, synthetic/Petrobras, Miranga clastic and SF-30 clastic. Ekofisk: 43 cm near drawdown, observed casing problem. SF-30 Sabah: 5.9 cm, no impact. Field X: 0.5 cm, no potential impact. Fault location/material/loading and observed versus predicted outcomes differ. Ratios are numeric comparisons, not risk-reduction factors. Body says Table 12; this is Table 5.

Ekofisk average strain 2.0–3.5%; Matagorda 2.1–3.25% headline. All casing, sand, gravel-pack and completion-failure descriptions inspected, including 0.25–1.25% incremental average strain for catastrophic Phase II failures. Those metrics are distinct from Field X local maximum equivalent strain. SPE 17856/84553 are unresolved originals; no universal 2% safety threshold.

equations.expression: P_injection > Shmin: textual fracture-propagation condition; 4600−4000=600psi (analyst arithmetic)
equations.units: psi as printed; gauge/absolute and datum unspecified
equations.assessment: Textual threshold and chosen margin. No complete fracture propagation, tensile-strength, thermal/chemical or capillary model is supplied. The 600 psi difference applies to the lower reported Shmin. The reservoir-pressure recommendation is not explicitly a flowing-BHP control.

equations.expression: Missing: poroelastic horizontal strain, equilibrium/coupling, ISAMGEO cap/yield/flow/hardening/creep, Mohr–Coulomb frictional contact and fracture/leakage laws
equations.assessment: Named methods do not supply their complete derivations or implementation. No unprovided formula is attributed to the authors or substituted as full reproduction.

variables: Phi: porosity in Tables 1–2. Fraction/percent scale, possible table-to-table convention change and valid fit range are not defined. ln requires a positive dimensionless argument. Analyst examples do not resolve the intended convention.

RHOB: bulk density, g/cc. YME: Young modulus, Mpsi. PR: Poisson ratio, dimensionless. UCS/TSTR: unconfined compressive/tensile strength, psi. FANG/DANG: friction/dilation angles, degrees. The Mpsi label is preserved; dynamic/static conversion and lithology-specific calibration remain unavailable.

Pc_exp: preconsolidation pressure, Psi. H_exp: hardening parameter, unitless. Rat0: plastic volumetric strain reference rate, labelled unitless. BRat0: rate-dependent pore-collapse exponent, unitless. Reference time, stress normalisation and sign/domain restrictions are missing.

The UPVC p–q and porosity/volumetric-strain paths are described, not supplied. Stress-invariant definitions, compression sign, Biot coefficient and total/effective-stress connection need the native laws/tests.

Sh/SH: minimum/maximum horizontal stress. Table 3 gives 0.78 psi/ft, SH/Sh=1.04 and Sh azimuth 110°; prose gives SH N20°E. Vertical stress and depth datum are missing. Figure 15 total-XX output needs rotation/principal-stress mapping.

Reservoir pressure is labelled psi without absolute/gauge or spatial datum. Preserve the 4,000 psi recommendation, 4,600–6,200 psi Shmin and 600 psi margin. No EOS conversion, flowing BHP or annual rate is inferred.
Seawater pressure gradient 0.45 psi/ft is an initialization input; it is not CO2 density, a flow pressure loss or a complete pore-pressure field.

Figure 3 MD (ft), inclination/azimuth (degrees), stress (psi), modulus (Mpsi), mud gradient (ppg), bit/caliper (inches) and casing shoes are distinct. MD cannot be treated as TVD/SSTVD. Some tiny labels and channel definitions require native exports.
Four MEMs, approximately two million cells, 23 selected stress states and 4-D time are structural metadata. Counts provide neither probabilities nor annual flow schedules.
Prose gives positive subsidence magnitudes; Figures 8–10 show negative displacement. Platform/seabed/reservoir, survey/model differences and reference epochs must remain distinct.

Fault stiffness is psi/ft, stress per displacement, not a modulus in psi. Adopted SF-30 clastic values: 66,311/30,945 psi/ft normal/shear stiffness, 217.5 psi cohesion, 15° friction. These are not Field X fault measurements.

Fault slip/deformation is cm; 0.5 cm=5 mm. Local plastic strain 2%=0.02 is not a failure probability or foreign-field average/incremental volumetric compaction. Crest porosity above 30% is not volume-average porosity.
Twelve overburden faults, four named/displayed faults (1,5,7,10) and five affected faults in the conclusion remain distinct assertions. A fifth identity is unresolved.

Production 1995, depletion end 2003, prediction 2013, GPS 2014, proposed injection 2024 and forecast endpoint 2040 distinguish observations, calibration and forecasts. Asynchronous differences are not RMSE or availability.

Full thermal/chemical/seepage/capillary/cement pathways, strength degradation, post-closure horizon and carbon mass balance are not disclosed or independently reproduced. Small mechanical increments cannot supply leakage probability or permanent retention.

claims.claim: Workflow reduces cost/time and supports capacity/safety
claims.assessment: Methodological aims; no comparative time/cost baseline, numeric capacity or post-closure retention result. Full alternative injection cases are not supplied.

claims.claim: Property, GPS and bathymetry agreement validates predictions
claims.assessment: Calibration and qualitative matches are presented with iterative pore-collapse/creep fitting. Independent holdouts and errors are unavailable. A 2013 prediction and 2014 observation are not a matched validation pair.

claims.claim: About 1 ft uplift and final 10.6/16 ft seabed/reservoir deformation
claims.assessment: Conditional forecasts. Unit conversions replay magnitudes only. Platform histories, spatial maxima and creep/injection epochs differ; deformation alone cannot supply working storage or annual rate.

claims.claim: About 0.5 cm slip mainly during depletion; little injection effect
claims.assessment: The model uses deformation as a contact-strain workaround with imported clastic properties. Small slip and no reported historical casing problem do not prove zero future failure or leakage. Four-versus-five fault count remains open.

claims.claim: Stress rotation matters for trajectory optimisation
claims.assessment: A qualitative map/caption. No numeric rotation, failure envelope, objective/constraints or validated selected trajectory is supplied.

claims.claim: About 2% highest strain and little injection increment imply low failure risk
claims.assessment: Local maximum equivalent strain differs from other fields’ average compaction measures. Table 6 also reports catastrophic failures at smaller incremental averages. Original metrics and mechanisms require verification; no universal 2% criterion.

claims.claim: 4,000 psi reservoir recommendation with 600 psi safety margin
claims.assessment: The lower 4,600 psi stress gives 600 psi difference; the upper 6,200 gives 2,200. The ratio is 13.04% of lower Shmin or 15% of the recommendation. Pressure/datum, BHP, fracture/coupling law and uncertainty remain missing. Pressure alone does not establish annual mass service.

claims.claim: A 2024 injection start and the scenario establish feasibility
claims.assessment: A future assumption in a 2019 publication, not evidence of actual operations in 2024–2026. No verified injection rate/mass history or current project identity is supplied.

Page 11 excludes a cement-bond/casing-caprock leakage pathway. Mechanical strain/slip/pressure assessment is not a mass leakage or permanence model. Pathways, flux, probability and retained-carbon horizon remain open.

reproduction: audit_malaysia_geomechanics.py produces 77 limited checks, including 44 evaluations of eleven transcribed correlations at analyst-selected numeric Phi arguments. It also checks pressure/distance/stiffness units, axis orthogonality, margin denominators and slip/count distinctions. It does not choose the unpublished Phi convention or reproduce reservoir, finite-element, ISAMGEO creep, fault-contact, fracture, leakage or cost models. Six explicit missing-input rows stay null. paper1_use: Retain Field X as an anonymous Central Luconia/Sarawak carbonate scenario. Its 4,000 psi reservoir recommendation and 600 psi lower-end stress difference are not flowing BHP, a transferable fracture limit or an annual maximum-rate series. The planned 2024 start is a 2019 scenario, not evidence of actual injection. Small computed slip and calibrated subsidence do not establish permanent retention, failure probability or net GHG. Do not join to other Malaysian Field X cases without identity evidence.
